dana (Finance Lead): Heads-up: temporary org-wide budget hold for Q3 planning. Details below — pls RT if you own vendor renewals.
dana (Finance Lead): Effective immediately, were applying an 8% holdback on all discretionary spend requests for the upcoming fiscal quarter to align with updated revenue guidance. This is not a freeze on mission-critical infra or committed contracts.
claire (Sourcing): quick clarify: does holdback mean we should delay new subscriptions or still submit POs and expect normal routing?
dana (Finance Lead): Submit as usual. Requests will be reviewed with the hold applied to non-critical line items. If a request is business-critical, mark "critical" on the procurement form and include a 1par justification.
luke (Eng Manager): our third-party embedding vendor renewal is $9.5k due May 4. Is that considered committed (no hold) or still subject to review?
claire (Sourcing): tagging procurement flow: Renewals with existing contractual obligations (signed contracts) are out of scope. Anything auto-renewing without contract needs a quick check. @luke if you have a PO or signed SOW, it should be processed.
ella (Sales): Small note for revenue ops: were seeing more requests for demo SaaS tools under $2k. Are we changing micro-purchase limits?
dana (Finance Lead): Micro-purchase policy unchanged for now: under $2,500 can use department p-card with Concur note + project code. However, holdback may reduce available discretionary budget — so teams should prioritize.
devops-bot: Automated reminder: Vendor exception form -> https://confluence.redwood/procurement/vendor-exception (use for >$10k non-standard approvals).
claire (Sourcing): New vendor path: any new vendor > $10k must complete Vendor Risk quick-check and Sourcing approval. For one-off exceptions to the holdback, use vendor-exception and select "budget-hold exception".
luke (Eng Manager): if we need a fast exception (embedding impacts prod), what's the SLA?
dana (Finance Lead): Exception SLA: 24h triage during business hours for infra-critical requests (include logs / incident link if applicable). For non-critical exceptions expect 3-5 business days.
ella (Sales): Also—virtual card mapping change? We had a couple of charges that landed on team cards but need to be routed to client cost centers.
claire (Sourcing): Were rolling an update to virtual-card mapping next week. If you anticipate recharges to clients, flag in the procurement form with "recharge-code" and finance will prioritize mapping before charge posts.
dana (Finance Lead): Quick checklist Ill paste in #general: 1) Submit procurement/PO as usual. 2) Mark "critical" for infra/committed contracts. 3) For new vendors > $10k, run quick-check. 4) For holdback exceptions use vendor-exception form. 5) Micro-purchases < $2,500: p-card + Concur note.
luke (Eng Manager): thanks dana, well gather PO and attach SOW.
ella (Sales): noted, will tell RevOps and Client Ops.
claire (Sourcing): I'll send a short Loom walkthrough for the vendor-exception flow and update the playbook page.
dana (Finance Lead): Thanks all. I know this is extra admin; goal is to preserve runway while minimizing impact to customer-facing and production systems. Ping me or @claire if you need help. :pray:
